exhibits.title: Why the answer is a conditional go
exhibits.subtitle: Vietnam coffee and tea chains · evidence as of 2025-26
rows: The pool is large and growing
Coffee chains USD 725m, tea chains USD 617m in 2025, both up 27-28% [MW 2026]; chain outlets 2.5x since 2019 [b-company 2025]
Room for a new brand without a price war, if it avoids the budget tier
Highlands 985 stores after 134 openings in 2025 [JFC 2025]; Milano about 2,500 outlets [MW 2026]; Mixue drinks at VND 10-30k [Mixue 2025]
Rules out a budget-coffee format: it would meet the strongest incumbents at their cost advantage
Drink-only 77% of visits; food lifts the ticket to VND 162k; Phuc Long, the best at food, attaches it on 28% of orders [Q&Me 2026]
Lead with bakery and dessert; price drinks in line with Katinat and Phuc Long
Store economics are tight but workable
Break-even near VND 16m a day; Phuc Long averaged VND 22.8m in 2025 [Masan 2025] [Kira estimates]
Only top-quartile sites work: site access decides the case
Café services open to full foreign ownership [WTO Schedule 2007]; sugar excise 8% from 2027 [SCT Law 2025]
No licence partner is needed; a partner is chosen for sites, not permission

exhibits.title: Rules that shape a café-chain entry
exhibits.subtitle: Vietnam · in force or enacted as of Oct 2026
rows: Café and restaurant services are open to 100% foreign ownership [WTO Schedule 2007]
No licence partner needed; a wholly owned or majority JV entity is possible
Each outlet needs a food-safety eligibility certificate before trading
Build licence lead time into every opening plan
A foreign franchisor registers with the trade ministry before granting franchises
Needed only for a master-franchise or sub-franchise route
Decree 342/2026 replaces Decree 09/2018 from 18 Oct 2026 and narrows the economic-needs test [Decree 342/2026]
Matters only if the chain also retails packaged goods; confirm with counsel
8% from 1 Jan 2027, 10% from 2028, on drinks above 5 g sugar per 100 ml [SCT Law 2025]
Bottled lines are in scope; scope for fresh-made drinks is unclear
Region-I minimum wage VND 5.31m a month from 1 Jan 2026 [Decree 293/2025]
Low base, but turnover and training are the real cost
Negotiate terms before launch; cap delivery at 35% of sales
exhibits.source: Source: as tagged per row; non-numeric process rules from public legal guidance

exhibits.title: What would have to be true
exhibits.subtitle: Vietnam café-chain entry · confidence = KIRA judgement
rows: Pilot stores hold VND 22m+ a day for six months after opening
Sets a three-year payback; the leaders' 2025 averages bracket it at about 17 and 22.8
Three pilot stores; weekly POS read-out from month 1
Lifts the ticket to about VND 94.5k; chain average is 23%
Pastry-case and combo tests in the pilot
Rent at or below 16% of sales on 5-year leases
Rent is the largest fixed cost and the main reason outlets fail
Partner's site list priced against plan sales before signing
Delivery at or below 35% of sales, at 22% or less effective fee
Above that, app fees erase the margin gain from food
Terms with both leading apps agreed before launch
A partner with 15+ suitable sites and no café brand
Site access is the binding constraint; conflicts kill priority
Long-list of 15; receptivity calls in the first 90 days
A menu that stays two drops ahead of copycats
Katinat-style fast followers will match signature drinks
Six-to-eight-week drop calendar; track copy lag

exhibits.title: Risk register for a café-chain entry
exhibits.subtitle: Vietnam · 1-5 scales · KIRA judgement · sorted by score
rows: Sales fade after the opening buzz
Gate on month-4 to month-9 sales, not launch weeks
Lock first sites before the 2027 listing
Signature menu copied within a season
Lead with food; drop calendar every 6-8 weeks
Partner misaligned on sites or pace
Site pipeline and exit terms written into the JV
Own ordering app; cap delivery at 35% of sales
Blend and hedge through a local roaster
Sugar excise extended to fresh drinks
